questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: James Cook University, JCU, is a well renowned institution within the field of marine biology, and with its location adjacent to the Great Barrier Reef there was no doubt this was the place I wanted to go.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather easy. All staff were incredibly helpful and they sent out heaps of material to prepare you for your arrival to the uni. I also participated in a pre arrival zoom meeting with the other internationals in which the international students team at JCU welcomed us and went through everything we needed to know prior to coming there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: JCU staff were incredibly helpful and inviting to the international students which made settling in very easy which was lovely. We were showed around campus and they pointed out the education central where you could get your student ID and receive help with course planning. They also offered brush up courses in the intro week, however, I only participated in the social events during this week. There were introductions to the social sports, fitness, quizzes, and speed friending events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my off campus accommodation through 'JCU Townsville Accommodation' on Facebook. There are frequently new posts about housing close to uni so keep an eye out here if you want to live off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I lived in Douglas with five Australian girls who all mostly kept to themselves, which was not ideal for me, but the house was very close to uni so I could easily bike there and join activities on campus.
I found housing after I had arrived. I stayed the first week in a hostel down in the city and the following week I did a short stay on 'George Roberts Hall' which is part of the on campus accommodation. I recommend skipping the hostel and going straight for the on campus short stay, cause then you get all the intro parties and events to get to know other people. If you like living on campus, chances are there will be a permanent room available quite fast on campus, or you can find a place off campus.
When choosing your neighborhood, most people say go for Douglas or Annandale as Aitkenvale has a rather dodgy reputation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Keep a thorough eye on your KU mail. I got a lot of information here, and when you follow the instructions given it's very straight forward. I applied pre approvals for a number of courses at both JCU and KU and then I chose the ones that fit together timetable wise in the eStudent portal. You select the courses and then you register for classes. They tell you all about it and I also got lots of help at the education central desk on campus because I chose to change subjects at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could easily get answers to your questions by email or simply by hopping down to the education central on campus. Lovely staff.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just keep a close eye on your KU email, your JCU email when you get one of those, and on deadlines for subject registration as some subjects are really popular.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fantastic professors for the most part. Good practice of academic writing, poster making, and presentations. They really value and emphasize these classic academic skills which we practiced a lot throughout the semester.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were at an appropriate level. Assessment is spread out over the semester with grading of reports and presentations that contribute to your grade. This means that the final exams are typically no more than 30/40 % of your grade and they are typically easier than exams at KU. However, the workload is spread out over the entire semester, and the assignments took more energy than what I've experienced at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to the workload I was used to at KU there were way more written assignments at JCU. Although the workload was fairly small in the beginning of the semester it really peaked towards the end of the semester with at least one big report and or presentation every week. I cannot stress enough how happy you will be to have EndNote or another reference program handy. I didn't use it before coming to JCU, but the amount of reports and time spent on it just made it worth while to get EndNote. The librarians were very helpful with downloading and introducing me to it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Aquatic Animal Ecophysiology
Ecological and Conservation Genetics
Coral Reef Ecology
Marine Conservation Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Aquatic Animal Ecophysiology was a super cool subject. Jan Strugnell who taught the course was an absolutely great professor. Cool practicals taking blood samples from live fish and dissecting fish as well. 
Marine Conservation was really cool, covering all things marine conservation, deeply rooted in current research. Geoff Jones was the course coordinator, however, he will not be next year, so I don't know how much the course will change.
Ecological and Conservation genetics was an incredibly demanding and a bit stressful course. Although I now, at the other side of it, can see that I have learnt a lot, it was just a lot of pressure during the semester. The subject is built around a single report about koala genetics, and throughout the semester we used seven different kinds of software to analyse SNP data. Very directed at hands on genetics, so if you're into that I say go for it. Otherwise, I say not worth it on an exchange semester, as it was too much to deal with while taking in the rest of the experience.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent a lot of money on diving and weekend trips as Townsville itself is not the most inspiring city to spend all your time. I also had to pay for a lab coat for Aquatic Animal Ecophysiology (200 DKK) and a field trip with Coral Reef ecology (1700 DKK).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than I had anticipated. However, the on campus options for grocery shopping are quite limited. Instead there are many cafes and food stalls so to avoid spending all my money there, I did weekly shopping trips to Stockland with the bus to buy groceries which made it easier to keep my budget.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the JCUSA social sports and played Beach Volleyball every monday. That was super fun and at an okay price - 370 DKK for the semester. There's an on campus fitness for those who enjoy that also at a fair rate I believe. The uni bar was open most Fridays and it was alright too.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every Tuesday there was Café International arranged by JCU. They served free coffee and snacks and had some kind of event on. Almost all international students would show up and it was always really nice to catch up with people or have a chat with the staff. They were really looking out for the wellbeing of their students. Often times on campus there was free food somewhere so keep an eye out!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely go for social sports. It was really fun and a great way to mingle.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I personally spent many weekends on Magnetic Island just a 20 minute ferry ride away from Townsville city centre. I also spent some of my weekends SCUBA diving with the JCU Dive Club on liveaboards which was absolutely incredible. 
Daytrip to Wallaman Falls is also a great activity. 
I also went to Cairns for a weekend - went over to Fitzroy Island, big recommendation! 
A lot of people also went to Airlie Beach for a weekend. In general just explore the options with the Greyhound bus up and down the coast if you're not getting a car.
The lagoon is just a 15 min bike ride from uni which is lovely for an after uni dip in the pool on week days.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Australian people were incredibly open, helpful, and welcoming. The only thing that was really different is they always ask you how you're doing at the beginning of any interaction which is very unlike danish people to do.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I met local students at the speed friending event at the beginning of the semester and in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their open-mindedness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) You'll be writing a fair bit of reports but that's alright - just get EndNote!
2) Make the most of your weekends.
3) Join the dive club on as many of their events as possible. If you're not a diver yet, get certified as early in the semester as possible. Many of the international students there regretted not doing it. There's so much fantastic diving in Australia.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are really into living in the middle of a big and busy city, Townsville is not the place for you. It's a rather small city and campus is located 12 km from the city centre so you'll have to take the bus or get a car. However, if you are good at making the most of your weekends, there are some amazing places close to the city to explore - and beautiful Magnetic island is always just 20 minutes away.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: A lot of really inspirational professors, cool practicals, and a lot of beautiful scuba diving!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the Ecological and Conservation genetics class. Quite the workload!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Definitely a great place to go if you're into marine biology! If I were to go again I would opt for on campus accommodation to be part of the social activities at the dorms, seeing as how the city centre was quite far from uni.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
